_comment: Written by oceanspill-model-status from the training runs. Do not edit by hand.

sarSegmentation.task: Finds oil pixels in Sentinel-1 and EOS-04 radar scenes
sarSegmentation.architecture: U-Net, 2 input channels (co-polarised and cross-polarised backscatter in decibels)
sarSegmentation.training: Sentinel-1 oil spill scenes with hand-drawn masks, plus look-alike and clean-sea scenes as negatives
sarSegmentation.note: Not trained yet; no accuracy figures.

opticalSegmentation.task: Finds oil in Sentinel-2 optical scenes, where radar look-alikes behave differently
opticalSegmentation.architecture: U-Net, 4 input channels (10 m blue, green, red and near-infrared reflectance)
opticalSegmentation.training: MADOS marine debris and oil spill scenes, fifteen hand-labelled classes
opticalSegmentation.dataset: MADOS (Marine Debris and Oil Spill), Sentinel-2
opticalSegmentation.falseAlarmBasis: 59 of 565 tiles with no target in them produced a detection of at least 50 pixels

shipDetection.task: Finds vessels in radar imagery, including ships transmitting nothing on AIS
shipDetection.architecture: U-Net, single-channel radar amplitude; connected regions become vessel detections
shipDetection.training: SAR Ship Detection Dataset, ship outlines rasterised from the annotations
shipDetection.falseAlarmBasis: 45 of 400 tiles with no target in them produced a detection of at least 50 pixels

drift.source: NOAA Global Drifter Program hourly product (doi 10.25921/x46c-3620)

spread.verdict: the measured 564 m²/s reproduces the observed spreading to within 34% on average; the model's old 8 m²/s is off by 85%

aisGaps.source: Global Fishing Watch published AIS disabling events (gaps judged intentional)
aisGaps.caveat: Confirmed disabling events only. Without a comparable sample of ordinary gaps from the same feed there is no base rate here, so a high percentile means 'resembles the deliberate ones', not 'probably deliberate'.
